actions.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

dimensions.assessment: Affects professional boxers, unified boxing organizations, promoters, managers, state athletic commissions, and ringside medical personnel nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: allow a professional boxer to choose to participate in the alternative system offered by a unified boxing organization

dimensions.assessment: Imposes detailed safety, medical examination, anti-doping, insurance, minimum compensation, and contract duration standards for professional boxing participants.
dimensions.evidence: to further enhance safety precautions that protect the well-being of professional boxers

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes the Federal Trade Commission to assess fees to offset costs of processing required filings from unified boxing organizations.
dimensions.evidence: assess the unified boxing organization a fee to offset the costs the Commission incurs in processing the information

dimensions.assessment: Amends multiple sections of the Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996, creating new statutory requirements for medical testing, anti-doping, contract limits, and organizational oversight.
dimensions.evidence: The Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996 (15 U.S.C. 6301 et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendments taking effect upon enactment and applying to matches held 180 days thereafter.
dimensions.evidence: take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act and shall apply with respect to professional boxing matches that take place on or after the date that is 180 days after such date of enactment

missing_information: Exact fee amounts the Federal Trade Commission may charge unified boxing organizations.
importance_detail.rationale: Amends the Professional Boxing Safety Act of 1996 to establish a comprehensive alternative regulatory framework for unified boxing organizations, adding strict medical, anti-doping, contract, and financial safety requirements.
